description: Canonical tool registry for SynqLab. Each entry includes fetch URL, model size, and description for programmatic integration.

sequence_representation.label: Sequence Representation
sequence_representation.purpose: Encode amino acid sequences into embeddings capturing evolutionary, structural, and functional properties.

tools.name: ESM-1b
tools.description: Transformer protein language model trained on UniRef50. Produces per-residue and per-sequence embeddings. Strong baseline for downstream tasks.

tools.name: ESM-2
tools.description: Updated ESM series with improved scaling and training. Recommended default for embeddings in SynqLab. The 650M checkpoint is a practical balance between quality and compute.

tools.name: ProtBERT
tools.description: BERT-based model trained on BFD and UniRef100. Accepts space-separated amino acids. Useful for classification and embedding tasks.

tools.name: ProtT5-XL
tools.description: T5-based encoder-decoder trained on UniRef50. High-quality per-residue embeddings. Larger memory footprint; use fp16 or offloading for inference.

tools.name: UniRep
tools.description: Multiplicative LSTM trained on UniRef50. One of the first transfer learning models for proteins. Lightweight; suitable for fast feature extraction.

tools.name: TAPE
tools.description: Benchmarking suite with pretrained models (BERT, LSTM, Transformer, ResNet) for protein tasks. Useful for establishing baselines in SynqLab evaluations.

tools.name: ESM-IF
tools.description: Inverse folding model from Meta. Also used as a structure-aware sequence encoder. Generates sequence likelihoods conditioned on backbone coordinates.

sequence_generation.label: Sequence Generation
sequence_generation.purpose: Generate novel protein or peptide sequences via language models or diffusion over sequence/structure space.

tools.name: ProGen
tools.description: Autoregressive protein language model conditioned on taxonomic and functional keywords. ProGen2 variants available at multiple scales. Suitable for conditional generation in SynqLab.

tools.name: ProtGPT2
tools.description: GPT-2 trained on UniRef50 protein sequences. Unconditional generative model; outputs natural-like sequences. Easy to fine-tune with LoRA for task-specific generation.

tools.name: EvoDiff
tools.description: Microsoft diffusion framework over protein sequences. Supports unconditional, motif-scaffolded, and inpaint generation. Good for diversity-controlled generation in exploration phases.

tools.name: RFdiffusion
tools.description: Diffusion model over protein backbone structure (not sequence). Generates backbone geometries de novo or around motifs; pair with ProteinMPNN to recover sequences. Key tool for structure-conditioned design.

tools.name: PepMLM
tools.description: Masked language model fine-tuned for peptide binder design conditioned on a target protein sequence. Directly relevant to GFP11 variant generation in SynqLab.

tools.name: TaxDiff
tools.description: Diffusion model conditioned on taxonomic labels to guide generation toward biologically plausible sequence families. Useful for diversity-controlled exploration.

structure_prediction.label: Structure Prediction
structure_prediction.purpose: Predict 3D atomic coordinates from amino acid sequence; model protein-protein and protein-ligand complexes.

tools.name: AlphaFold2
tools.description: DeepMind's landmark structure predictor achieving near-experimental accuracy for single chains. Requires MSA and template search pipeline. High-confidence pLDDT and PAE scores used as evaluation metrics.

tools.name: AlphaFold3
tools.description: Extended to predict complexes involving proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, and small molecules. Uses diffusion-based structure generation internally. Broader scope than AF2.

tools.name: AlphaFold-Multimer
tools.model_size: ~93M parameters (same backbone as AF2, fine-tuned for complexes)
tools.description: Fine-tuned AF2 for protein-protein complex prediction. Provides iPTM and pTM confidence scores used as in-silico proxies for interface quality in SynqLab evaluation.

tools.name: RoseTTAFold
tools.description: Three-track network (1D sequence, 2D distance, 3D coordinates) from Baker lab. Faster than AF2 at inference; pairs well with RFdiffusion for full design pipelines.

tools.name: ESMFold
tools.description: Single-sequence structure predictor requiring no MSA. Very fast (seconds per sequence). Ideal for large-scale screening in SynqLab's triage step.

tools.name: OmegaFold
tools.description: Single-sequence predictor using a protein language model foundation. No MSA or database lookup required. Fast alternative to ESMFold for screening.

tools.name: OpenFold
tools.description: Fully open-source reimplementation of AlphaFold2 with trainable weights. Enables fine-tuning and LoRA adaptation of AF2 components within SynqLab's closed-loop update step.

inverse_folding.label: Inverse Folding
inverse_folding.purpose: Design amino acid sequences compatible with a given 3D backbone structure.

tools.name: ProteinMPNN
tools.description: Message-passing neural network operating on backbone graphs (Cα, N, C, O). High experimental success rates. Primary inverse folding tool in SynqLab for sequence recovery from RFdiffusion backbones.

tools.name: LigandMPNN
tools.description: Extends ProteinMPNN to be aware of ligand and small molecule context at the binding site. Use when designing sequences around a known ligand or receptor pocket.

tools.name: Fold2Seq
tools.description: Transformer-based inverse folding model from Microsoft. Generates sequence distributions given a fold. Alternative to ProteinMPNN for ablation studies.

tools.name: DenseCPD
tools.description: Uses a 3D convolutional approach over voxelized protein environments for sequence design. Provides an alternative architecture for inverse folding.

docking.label: Interaction Prediction / Docking
docking.purpose: Predict binding poses and interaction modes between proteins, peptides, and ligands.

tools.name: DiffDock
tools.description: Diffusion generative model for protein-ligand docking. Frames docking as a generative problem over ligand pose space. Strong benchmark results; fast inference.

tools.name: DiffDock-PP
tools.description: Extension of DiffDock for rigid protein-protein docking. Directly relevant to GFP11/GFP1-10 complex prediction in SynqLab.

tools.name: RosettaDock
tools.description: Classical physics-based docking within the Rosetta suite. Optimizes interface energy; can incorporate experimental constraints (e.g., NMR, SAXS). Reference method for benchmarking.

tools.name: AutoDock Vina
tools.description: Widely used open-source small-molecule docking tool. Fast and well-validated. Useful for protein-ligand docking tasks in SynqLab pipelines.

tools.name: HADDOCK
tools.description: Data-driven docking platform that integrates experimental restraints (mutagenesis, NMR, cryo-EM). Web server and local install available. Good for complex modeling with prior knowledge.

tools.name: EquiBind
tools.description: Geometric deep learning model for direct-shot protein-ligand binding structure prediction. Very fast (milliseconds). Use for large-scale screening before expensive physics-based docking.

tools.name: TankBind
tools.description: Trigonometry-aware non-local network for protein-ligand binding prediction. Predicts binding site and pose simultaneously. Competitive with DiffDock on several benchmarks.

property_prediction.label: Property Prediction / Scoring
property_prediction.purpose: Evaluate thermodynamic stability, binding affinity, and mutational effects to rank and triage candidates.

tools.name: FoldX
tools.description: Empirical force field for fast ΔΔG prediction of mutations and interactions. Industry standard for stability estimation. Requires registration for academic use.

tools.name: Rosetta3
tools.description: Comprehensive macromolecular modeling suite. Provides energy scoring (Rosetta energy units), design, and docking. Reference tool for stability and affinity scoring.

tools.name: PyRosetta
tools.description: Python API wrapping the Rosetta3 suite. Enables programmatic scoring, minimization, and design. The primary interface for integrating Rosetta into SynqLab pipelines.

tools.name: DeepDDG
tools.description: Neural network predicting ΔΔG of protein stability upon single-point mutations from sequence and structural features. Fast alternative to FoldX for large mutational scanning.

tools.name: mCSM
tools.description: Graph-based signature approach for predicting mutation effects on stability and protein-protein interactions. Available as a web server and standalone tool.

tools.name: DynaMut
tools.model_size: N/A (ensemble of Normal Mode Analysis + graph signatures)
tools.description: Combines normal mode analysis with mCSM graph signatures to predict stability changes from mutations. Captures dynamic flexibility effects not modeled by static energy functions.

tools.name: GraphSite
tools.description: Graph neural network for binding site prediction from protein structure. Used in SynqLab to identify candidate interaction surfaces before docking.

molecular_simulation.label: Molecular Simulation
molecular_simulation.purpose: Run physics-based MD simulations to validate structural stability and conformational dynamics beyond static structure prediction.

tools.name: GROMACS
tools.description: High-performance MD engine optimized for biomolecular simulations. Widely used GPU-accelerated option. Default simulation backend in SynqLab for top-k candidate validation.

tools.name: OpenMM
tools.description: Python-native MD library with flexible force field and integrator API. Ideal for programmatic integration into SynqLab pipelines. Supports CUDA, OpenCL, and CPU platforms.

tools.name: NAMD
tools.description: Parallel MD engine from UIUC. Highly scalable for large systems on HPC clusters. Supports CHARMM and AMBER force fields.
tools.license: UIUC Open Source (free for academic use)

tools.name: AMBER
tools.description: Comprehensive molecular dynamics package with widely validated AMBER force fields for proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules. Commercial license required.

tools.name: CHARMM
tools.description: Long-standing biomolecular simulation package with extensive scripting and analysis capabilities. The CHARMM force field is one of the most validated for protein simulations.
